subclassFluff.name: House Agent
entries: {@i Outwit Your Foes with Charm and Subterfuge}

subclassFluff.name: Imaskarcanist
entries: {@i Master the Secrets of Unlight and the Artifacts of Ancient Imaskar}

subclassFluff.name: Path of Unlight
entries: {@i Unleash your inner light as blazing fury}

entries.name: What is Unlight?
entries: The city of Deep Imaskar, home to the descendants of the ancient Imaskari empire, lies in one of the lowest levels of the Underdark. The Deep Imaskari wield a magical force known as Unlight, taught to them by {@i Imaskarcana}, sentient grimoires penned by ancient wizard-kings of the lost Imaskari empire.

The Deep Imaskari used Unlight to create the Great Seal, a magical symbol that protects and illuminates their city while nourishing crops that allow the Deep Imaskari to survive in the Underdark. But Unlight can also be used to corrupt and destroy, burning creatures from within until they die in a fiery explosion of brilliant light.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Unlight
entries: Barbarians infused with the power of Unlight embrace uncontrollable magic in exchange for incredible physical prowess. The Unlight burning inside them illuminates the darkness while burning and blinding the barbarian's enemies

Most barbarians on this path were first exposed to Unlight in the Underdark. The Deep Imaskari grant Unlight to chosen warriors who lead their army against the upper regions of the Underdark, and some of these soldiers have fled to pursue lives of their own. But the magic of Unlight is contagious and spreads in unpredictable ways. It infects people only briefly exposed to it and occasionally manifests in individuals who have never been to the Underdark.

subclassFeature.name: Radiant Rage
entries: The Unlight coursing through you fuels your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB}. If a creature hits you with a melee attack roll while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} is active, the creature takes Radiant damage equal to your Rage Damage bonus.
Additionally, while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} is active, you shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius.

subclassFeature.name: Unlight Manifestation
entries: Barbarians on the Path of Unlight manifest the radiant energy of Unlight when they rage, but this energy can take many forms. You can roll on or choose a result from the {@table Unlight Manifestation|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} table to inspire the form your {@subclassFeature Radiant Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|Unlight|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions|3|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} takes.

subclassFeature.name: Unlight Revelation
entries: You have {@variantrule proficiency|XPHB} in the {@skill Perception} skill, if you lack it. You also gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in that skill.

While your rage is active, you have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range equal to that of the {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} provided by your {@subclassFeature Radiant Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|Unlight|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions|3|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions}.

subclassFeature.name: Harbinger of Unlight
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Radiant damage.

subclassFeature.name: Infectious Unlight
entries: Damage you deal with {@classFeature Brutal Strike|Barbarian|XPHB|9|XPHB} can be Radiant or the usual type (your choice). The following effect is now among your {@classFeature Brutal Strike|Barbarian|XPHB|9|XPHB} options.

items.name: Radiant Infection
entries: The target becomes infected with Unlight for 1 minute. While infected, it sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius. Additionally, at the start of each of its turns, the target takes {@damage 1d6} Radiant damage. The target makes a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Strength modifier and {@table Proficiency Bonus|XPHB}) at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Brilliant Rage
entries: The aura of your Unlight is bolstered. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} is active, you shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you unleash blinding brilliance. When you do, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you makes a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Strength modifier and {@table Proficiency Bonus|XPHB}). On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 1d12} Radiant damage and has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage only.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend a use of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: House Agent
entries: The drow houses of Menzoberranzan conspire against each other in a great game of status and sabotage that expands far beyond the city's limits. When a house needs a specialized tool to further its interests without arousing suspicion, it calls in a house agent.
Using the tools and training of their sponsor, a house agent is a master infiltrator, capable of insinuating themself into their target's life and striking while their target's back is turned.

subclassFeature.name: Charming Presence
entries: You can take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Additionally, choose one of the following skills: {@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, or {@skill Performance|XPHB}, or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}. You have proficiency in that skill.

subclassFeature.name: House Insignia
entries: You gain a magical token in the form of a brooch or coin that marks you as an agent of your sponsor and that bears their heraldry. While you have this insignia, you can cast certain spells with it. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for spells you cast with your insignia.

items.name: Cantrips
entries: You learn the {@spell Friends|XPHB} cantrip.

items.name: Find Familiar
entries: You can cast the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell but only as a {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB}. Your sponsor provides the Material component for your first casting of this spell. You must choose the {@creature Spider|XMM} form for your familiar.

items.name: Insignia Spells
entries: When you reach a level specified in the {@table Insignia Spells|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} table, you learn the listed spells. Once you cast a spell using your insignia, you can't cast that spell again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Losing Your Insignia
entries: If you lose your insignia, your house finds a way to deliver you a new one, whether it is via a courier, a magical familiar, teleportation magic, or some other method. Your new insignia is delivered to you when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Loyalty Test
entries: Each house agent is required to prove their loyalty before their sponsor allows them into the inner circles of the organization. You can roll on or choose a result from the {@table House Agent Origins|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} table to inspire the incident that made you a full-fledged member of your house.

entries.name: Using Other Sponsors
entries: Though this Rogue is designed to work with the backing of a drow house of Menzoberranzan, a House Agent might instead have the backing of another large group. They could belong to a duergar clan, a religious order, or a faction such as Bregan D'Aerthe or the Zhentarim. Or your Rogue could have had multiple sponsors—perhaps they first worked for a drow house, then defected to serve another cause.

subclassFeature.name: Backstab
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures within 5 feet of you that are {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you or have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} Condition. You also gain the following {@classFeature Cunning Strike|Rogue|XPHB|5|XPHB} option.

items.name: Stunning Betrayal (Cost: {@dice 4d6})
entries: If your target was {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you or had the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition when you hit it, the target has the {@condition Stunned} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Infiltration Partner
entries: The familiar you have through the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell gains {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet and {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet.

Additionally, when you cast the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell or finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} while you have a familiar, you can grant your familiar {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@class Rogue|XPHB} level.

subclassFeature.name: Silver Tongue
entries: A creature's {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} attitude doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on your Charisma checks to influence that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Subtle Manipulator
entries: You gain the following {@classFeature Cunning Strike|Rogue|XPHB|5|XPHB} option.

items.name: Confound ({@dice 5d6})
entries: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to your spellcasting DC or have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save when it takes any damage, ending the effect on itself on a success

Additionally, you can cast the {@spell Friends|XPHB} spell as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. The target no longer automatically succeeds on the saving throw if it isn't a Humanoid or if you're fighting it.
Finally, when a spell you cast that gives a target the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition ends, the target doesn't know it was {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you.

subclassFeature.name: Imaskarcanist
entries: Imaskarcanists have learned the ancient secrets of Deep Imaskar, a once-human society living in the deepest depths of the Underdark. Through these eldritch arts—taught to the Deep Imaskari by sentient artifacts called the {@i Imaskarcana}—they have mastered the power of Unlight, a brilliant, destructive, and infectious energy that can be used to both heal and destroy. With this power, the Deep Imaskari have launched a war of conquest to bring light to every corner of the Underdark. Each Imaskarcanist must decide for themself whether to aid the conquering army or use their power against it and preserve the comforting darkness of the world below.

subclassFeature.name: Learning the Secrets of Unlight
entries: Unlight is a rare form of magic known to very few. You can roll on or choose a result from the {@table Secrets of Unlight|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} table to inspire how your character learned about this secret magic.

subclassFeature.name: Unlight Adept
entries: You know how to weave Unlight into your damaging spells. When you cast a spell that deals Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage, you can change that damage type to Radiant.
In addition, {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} created by spells you cast is {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} instead.

subclassFeature.name: Unlight Invigoration
entries: You can imbue creatures with Unlight drawn from your own energy, making them stronger and fiercer. As a {@variantrule Bonus action|XPHB}, choose a willing creature you can see within 30 feet of you and roll one or two of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}. Those dice are then expended. The target gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the total rolled plus your Intelligence modifier, and until the target has no {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks and sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius.

subclassFeature.name: Unlight Restoration
entries: You can wield the restorative effects of Unlight to heal injuries and remove harmful effects. As a {@variantrule Bonus action|XPHB}, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you and roll one or two of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}. Those dice are then expended. The target regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the total rolled and sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius until the end of its next turn.

If you expended two {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, you can choose to end one of the following conditions on the target: {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, or {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}. If you do, the target does not regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Secrets of Deep Imaskar
entries: Your research into the secrets of the Imaskarcana grants you the following benefits.

items.name: Imaskarcana Lore
entries: You can attune yourself to a magic item as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Piercing Unlight
entries: Your spells ignore {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Radiant damage.

items.name: Unlight Resilience
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Radiant damage.

items.name: Imaskar Seals
entries: You always have the {@spell Glyph of Warding|XPHB} spell prepared and can cast it once without a spell slot. When you cast the spell in this way, you don't need Material components, you cast the spell as if using a spell slot equal to the highest Wizard spell slot you have. Any previous glyph you created in this way is broken, and its spell ends without being triggered. You regain the ability to cast {@spell Glyph of Warding|XPHB} in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Doom Of Unlight
entries: You can curse your enemies with corrosive Unlight, and the only escape from the curse is physical violence or an explosive death.

When a creature takes Radiant damage from a spell you cast, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to curse that creature with Unlight. The creature makes a Constitution save against {@dcYourSpellSave}. On a failure, the creature is cursed. Until the curse ends, the target suffers the following effects:

items: The target emits {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius.
Attack rolls against the target have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.
At the start of each of the target's turns, it takes Radiant damage equal to your character level.
The target has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks and melee attack rolls.
If the target hits another creature with a melee attack roll, the target can repeat the Constitution save, ending this curse on a success.

If the target is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it explodes. Roll a number of {@dice d8|d8s} equal to half your character level. Creatures in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} centered on the target take Radiant damage equal to the total rolled.

entries: Once you have attempted to curse a creature using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} or until you expend a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

feat.name: Full Ceremorphosis
entries: You grow four tentacles around your mouth, your head elongates, and your skin becomes purple and slick with mucus. Your transformation into a mind flayer is complete. You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Psionic Energy Dice
entries: The Psionic Energy Dice granted to you by this feat path become d10s. If they are already d10s, they instead become d12s.

items.name: Aberration
entries: Your creature type is Aberration.

items.name: Illithid Specialization
entries: You excel at a particular illithid talent. Choose one of the following benefits:

items.name: Brain-Seeking Tentacles
entries: When you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can use both the Damage and the Grapple option. You can expend a Psionic Energy Die when you use this benefit to roll the expended die. The target takes extra Psychic damage equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier, and it subtracts half the number rolled (round up) from its saving throw to avoid gaining the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. If the target is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} as a result of this benefit, the Psionic Energy Die isn't expended. You can use this benefit only once per turn.

items.name: Mind Flayer Spells
entries: You always have the {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB}, {@spell Levitate|XPHB}, and {@spell Mind Blast|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} spells prepared. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells. You can cast these spells without expending a spell slot by expending a Psionic Energy Die. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of an appropriate level.

items.name: Repeatable
entries: You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different option for Illithid Specialization each time.

feat.name: Illithid Thrallmaker
entries: You have honed your psionic ability to become a master manipulator. You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Psionic Energy Dice
entries: The Psionic Energy Dice granted to you by this feat path become d8s.

items.name: Telepathy
entries: You have {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB} with a range of 10 feet. If you already have {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB}, your range increases by 10 feet.

items.name: Persuasive Presence
entries: You always have the {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell prepared. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell. You can cast it without expending a spell slot by expending a Psionic Energy Die. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. When you expend a Psionic Energy Die to cast the spell, roll the expended die. One target of the spell subtracts half the number rolled (round up) from its saving throw against the spell.

feat.name: Tadpole Host
entries: You begin a symbiotic relationship with the mind flayer tadpole in your body. You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Mind Sliver
entries: You learn the {@spell Mind Sliver|XPHB} cantrip. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

items.name: Psionic Power
entries: The wellspring of psionic energy provided to you by your tadpole is represented by Psionic Energy Dice, which fuel the powers you have from this feat path.

You have a number of Psionic Energy Dice equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. When you take this feat, your Psionic Energy Die is a {@dice d6}. The die changes when you take feats along the {@charoption Path of Ceremorphosis|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions}.

Any features in this feat path that use a Psionic Energy Die use only the dice from this feat path. Some of your features expend Psionic Energy Dice, as specified in a feature's description, and you can't use a feature if it requires you to use a die when all your Psionic Energy Dice are expended.
You regain all expended Psionic Energy Dice when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Psionic Overload
entries: Whenever you deal Psychic damage, you can expend a Psionic Energy Die to roll the die and deal extra Psychic damage equal to the number rolled.

feat.name: Tadpole's Safeguard
entries: Your tadpole has a vested interest in protecting its shell while it incubates. You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Psionic Energy Dice
entries: The Psionic Energy Dice granted to you by this feat path become d8s.

items.name: Telepathy
entries: You have {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB} with a range of 10 feet. If you already have {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB}, your range increases by 10 feet.

items.name: Warding Backlash
entries: You always have the {@item Shield|XPHB} spell prepared. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell. You can cast it without expending a spell slot by expending a Psionic Energy Die. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. When you expend a Psionic Energy Die to cast the spell and cause the triggering attack to miss, roll the expended die. The attacker takes Psychic damage equal to the number rolled.

feat.name: Ulitharid's Might
entries: The tadpole you ingested is mutating you into an {@creature ulitharid|MPMM}, a rare type of illithid that boasts great physical strength and mental power, as well as two additional tentacles.

items.name: Psionic Energy Dice
entries: The Psionic Energy Dice granted to you by this feat path become d8s.

items.name: Telepathy
entries: You have {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB} with a range of 10 feet. If you already have {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB}, the range increases by 10 feet.

items.name: Extended Tentacles
entries: Two long tentacles sprout from around your mouth. You can use these tentacles to make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. When you're using these tentacles, your reach increases by 5 feet.

charoption.name: Path of Ceremorphosis
entries: Ceremorphosis is the process by which {@creature mind flayer|XMM|mind flayers} create more mind flayers. They incubate their tadpole young in the tank that houses their colony's {@creature elder brain|MPMM}. When a tadpole is ready, they insert it into the body of a suitable host. During the transformative period that ensues, the host gains access to psychic powers even before the new illithid's more monstrous parts begin to develop.
The best hosts are typically humanoids capable of great physical, mental, and magical feats—in other words, adventurers.

entries.name: From Tadpole to Transformation
entries: Ceremorphosis is typically a parasitic relationship in which a tadpole eats the mind of its host and takes over the host's body. The resulting mind flayer retains the memories of its host but is an entirely different creature with its own thoughts and motivations. This mind flayer is subject to the will of an elder brain, a powerful leader of a mind flayer colony.

Ceremorphosis usually occurs quickly, but your path to becoming a mind flayer is different from traditional methods. As you take feats along this path, imagine what you might look like at every stage of this process. Your skin could turn a deeper violet with each feat you take, or your eyes might change color and shape.

Something prevents you from giving yourself over to the whims of the elder brain. Roll on or choose from the {@table Ceremorphosis Variables|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} table to inspire what protects you from this foul influence.

entries.name: Elder Brain Control
entries: Roleplaying the relationship between a burgeoning mind flayer and an elder brain can be a fun part of this path, but it requires a conversation with your DM. Whatever you decide, make sure both you and the DM agree on the terms of the relationship. Some topics you might discuss include the following:

items: How does the elder brain communicate with your character—through words, images, or impulses?
Is the elder brain open about its true nature, or does it pretend to be the character's deity or trusted ally?
What are the consequences for your character if they defy the elder brain's orders?
What, if anything, can the elder brain force your character to do? How does your character resist?

entries.name: Path of Ceremorphosis Feats
entries: The following Path of Ceremorphosis feats represent one path a character can take to become a mind flayer. To complete the Path of Ceremorphosis, begin by taking the {@feat Tadpole Host|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} feat, followed by any other Path of Ceremorphosis feat you choose. Finally, when you reach level 12 or higher, take the {@feat Full Ceremorphosis|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} feat.

entries.name: Mind Blast
entries: The {@feat Full Ceremorphosis|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} feat grants the {@spell Mind Blast|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions} spell, provided here:

spell.name: Mind Blast
entries: You unleash a concussive burst of psionic energy. Each creature in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} originating from you makes an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 6d8} Psychic damage and has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 6.

table.name: Ceremorphosis Variables
colLabels: You're Protected from the {@creature Elder Brain|MPMM} By...
rows: A blessing from your deity, given unconditionally.
The interference of an archdevil you've sold your soul to.
The elder brain's desire to see what happens if a host retains its autonomy.
A one-of-a-kind helm that the Society of Brilliance infused with Abjuration magic.
A mind and personality so awful that they deter the elder brain from interacting with you.
The interference of another elder brain vying for control over your mind.

table.name: House Agent Origins
rows: Taking the fall for another person's crime and serving their jail sentence.
Assassinating a powerful political figure.
Renouncing all personal ties and worldly possessions and adopting a new identity.
Uncovering an incriminating secret about a member of another house.
Withstanding a torturous interrogation without divulging house secrets.
Sacrificing a family member for the benefit of your sponsor.

table.name: Insignia Spells
rows: {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}
{@spell Suggestion|XPHB}
{@spell Hypnotic Pattern|XPHB}

table.name: Secrets of Unlight
rows: You were taught by a refugee from Deep Imaskar who brought this knowledge to the surface world.
You heard whispers in your dreams in a language you inexplicably understood.
You discovered written records left behind by a long-dead Imaskari wizard.
You were apprenticed to a Deep Imaskari wizard in the depths of the Underdark, but you escaped.
You heard rumors of this power from Underdark refugees, then pieced its secrets together through laborious research.
A mind flayer gave you notes salvaged from a Deep Imaskari whose brain the creature had eaten.

table.name: Unlight Manifestation
rows: White light blazing from your eyes and mouth.
Complex arcane symbols of light etched onto your body.
A cyclone of bright light that whirls around you.
Cracks in your flesh that reveal burning light within.
A ghostly form made of light that hovers above you.
Pale fire that dances on the tip of your weapon.

data.name: Unearthed Arcana 2026: Underdark Options
entries: This playtest document is part of a series of {@i Unearthed Arcana} articles that present material designed for upcoming products. The material here uses the rules in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}.

entries.name: What's Inside
entries: This document presents three new subclasses:
This document also includes a new transformative path of feats: the {@charoption Path of Ceremorphosis|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions}.

entries.name: Content Warning
entries: This material contains descriptions of body horror, damage to the eyes and brain, ingested parasites, and the idea that you are slowly losing control of yourself. Some readers might find this content disturbing.

entries.name: This Is Playtest Material
entries: This article is presented for playtesting and feedback. The options here are experimental and in draft form. They aren't officially part of the game. Your feedback will help determine whether we adopt it as official.

items.name: How to Playtest This UA
entries: We invite you to try out this material in play. To play with this material, you may either incorporate it into your campaign or run one or more special playtest sessions. For such a session, you may create an adventure of your own or use a short adventure from the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|3|Adventure Examples} or a source like {@adventure Dragon Delves|DrDe-BD}.

items.name: Power Level
entries: The character options you read here might be more or less powerful than options in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}. If a design survives playtesting, we adjust its power to the desirable level before publication. This means an option could be more or less powerful in its final form.

items.name: Feedback
entries: The best way for you to give us feedback on this material is in the survey we'll release on D&D Beyond. If we make this material official, it will be refined based on your feedback, and then it will appear in a D&D book.
Providing feedback on this document is one way you can help shape the future of D&D!

entries.name: Subclasses
entries: This section presents the following subclasses: {@class Barbarian|XPHB|Path of Unlight|Unlight|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions}, {@class Rogue|XPHB|House Agent|House Agent|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions}, and {@class Wizard|XPHB|Imaskarcanist|Imaskarcanist|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions}.

entries.name: Path of Unlight (Barbarian)
entries: {@i Unleash your inner light as blazing fury}

entries.name: What is Unlight?
entries: The city of Deep Imaskar, home to the descendants of the ancient Imaskari empire, lies in one of the lowest levels of the Underdark. The Deep Imaskari wield a magical force known as Unlight, taught to them by {@i Imaskarcana}, sentient grimoires penned by ancient wizard-kings of the lost Imaskari empire.

The Deep Imaskari used Unlight to create the Great Seal, a magical symbol that protects and illuminates their city while nourishing crops that allow the Deep Imaskari to survive in the Underdark. But Unlight can also be used to corrupt and destroy, burning creatures from within until they die in a fiery explosion of brilliant light.

entries.name: House Agent (Rogue)
entries: {@i Outwit Your Foes with Charm and Subterfuge}

entries.name: Imaskarcanist (Wizard)
entries: {@i Master the Secrets of Unlight and the Artifacts of Ancient Imaskar}

entries.name: Eldritch Invocations
entries: The following two Eldritch Invocations complement the {@class Warlock|XPHB|Primordial Patron|Primordial|XUA2026UnderdarkOptions}.
